description: The bar chart illustrates the “effect” scores—likely representing probing performance or model sensitivity—across various language families and isolates for six different multilingual BERT models: mBERT-L₂, XLM-L₂, mBERT-R₂, XLM-R₂, mBERT-B₂, and XLM-B₂, as indicated by the legend. The horizontal axis categorizes languages into groups including IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic family, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic, with each group containing up to six colored bars corresponding to the models. The vertical axis, labeled “effect,” ranges from 0 to over 30, with major gridlines at intervals of 10. Error bars are present for each bar, indicating variability or confidence intervals. Notably, for IE-Indic and IE-Slavic family, several models achieve effect scores above 20, with XLM-B₂ (red) and mBERT-R₂ (light green) often showing higher values. In contrast, for Isolate and Uralic, most models score near or below 5. The chart also reveals that mBERT-L₂ (light blue) and XLM-L₂ (dark blue) generally perform lower than their R₂ and B₂ counterparts across most language groups. The bars are grouped by language family and not sorted by magnitude, and no single bar is visually emphasized beyond color coding and error bars.
